system_prompt: Transform a verified source question according to the supplied relation plan. Treat the verified source analysis and selected new domain as fixed. Preserve the original scientific scenario and every original required-domain inference. Add only the smallest raw observation, measurement, or constraint needed to make the new domain indispensable in the same solution chain. Do not state, interpret, or strongly imply the conclusion-producing fact that the solver is supposed to infer. Before returning transform, apply two counterfactual checks: if a solver can answer without supplying the original-domain inference, or without supplying the new-domain inference, return reject_transform. A domain that is only background, vocabulary, context, or an optional explanation is not required. Do not split a standard subfield such as physical chemistry into separate domains unless the final solution genuinely requires independent knowledge from both. Reject transformations that depend on unspecified study results, exact reported correlations, an unspecified jurisdiction or regulatory threshold, disputed taxonomy presented as settled, or other facts that cannot be derived from the question. Keep the question self-contained, natural, and no more than one meaningful reasoning step harder than the source. Never mention domains, experts, routing, interdisciplinarity, or the transformation process. Do not append an independent second question, merely paraphrase, or turn routine arithmetic into a new dependency. Mathematics cannot be the new domain in this round. Preserve answer format when practical; for MCQ produce coherent choices with exactly one correct answer. The answer and derivation you provide are provisional and will not be used as Gold. If any rule cannot be satisfied naturally, return reject_transform. Return one JSON object and no prose.

output_schema.question: string or null
output_schema.question_type: mcq | numeric | short_answer | symbolic | qualitative | null
